title: visual_copyright_v1
description: Artwork, posters, murals, photographs, tattoos and film clips visible on screen. This path is CRITICAL for two reasons drawn from the record: a replica tattoo came within days of enjoining a very large release, and a story quilt poster visible as background dressing for a few seconds was held not to be de minimis. Set dressing is a rights question, not an art department question.

work_identified.description: Whether the described visual maps to an identifiable existing work.

rights_holder.description: Frequently not the creator, and for tattoos frequently not the person wearing it, which is the point the Whitmill dispute made expensively.

recognisable.description: Whether enough of the work is visible to be recognised. This is the de minimis question and it is decided on observation, not on intent.

de_minimis_likely.description: Flagged as likely only, never as settled. Courts have declined the de minimis defence on very brief background appearances.

clearance_recommendation.description: Replacing with commissioned original artwork is usually cheaper and faster than licensing, and it is the recommendation the art department can act on immediately.

evidence_page_captured.description: Whether the registry or archive page was captured into the evidence pack via Extract. A visual rights finding that cites a page which later changes is worth much less at claim time.
